name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

Only locked-view numbers appear in prose (496 cal, 40.7g protein, 34.4g carbs, 21.4g fat, 14 servings, 425 F, 30 + 10-15 min bake, 5 min rest, salt/pepper 1 1/2 tsp + 3/4 tsp). No numbers computed by writer.

prose.intro_html:
Lasagna usually shows up on the pricey, all-day-Sunday side of the recipe box, and it almost never shows up on the high-protein side. This one flips both. We take Alfredo, the sauce that normally turns a pan of noodles into a nap, and we build it on a base of blended cottage cheese so the whole thing comes out at 40.7 grams of protein a serving and still lands at 496 calories. That is the trick worth understanding: the creamy layer that tastes like a splurge is doing the protein heavy lifting.

You get breaded chicken bites, no-boil noodles, two real cheeses, and a sauce you make in a blender. It bakes in one shot, cools, and slices into 14 dinners that reheat like they were meant to. Comfort food that respects both your macros and your wallet. That is the entire pitch.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites and let them do the work. You need 2 lb 5 oz, and cooking them straight from frozen means no thawing window to plan around. Whatever bag size your store stocks, grab enough to clear that weight.

Cottage cheese is the quiet star here, so do not skip it for something fancier. You want 4 2/3 cups, which is a couple of standard tubs, and it goes into the blender where nobody will ever know it was cottage cheese. For the Alfredo, 1 3/4 cups of a jarred roasted garlic sauce keeps this simple; there is no reason to make a roux from scratch for a batch this size.

Get a block of fresh mozzarella to shred yourself (1 lb 2 1/2 oz) and grate your own Parmesan (2 1/3 cups, about 9 1/3 oz) rather than the pre-shredded bags. The blocks melt cleaner and you control the amount. Round out the cart with 21 no-boil lasagna sheets and a bunch of fresh parsley, since you only need 6 tbsp chopped and a small bunch covers that with garnish to spare.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 425 F. Bake or air fry the breaded chicken bites straight from frozen following the package directions, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces and set them aside.

Now the sauce, and this is where the protein hides. Add the cottage cheese, the Alfredo, and a generous pinch each of salt and pepper (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper across the batch) to a blender and run it until it is completely smooth. No lumps, no cottage cheese texture, just a creamy garlic sauce.

Assemble in layers. Because this is a 14-serving batch, spread it across two 13x9 dishes or one large deep pan. Start each dish with a thin coat of the blended sauce on the bottom so nothing sticks. Lay down 3 sheets of no-boil lasagna, then another layer of sauce, then chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and Parmesan. Repeat the layers until the dishes are full, and finish the top with mozzarella and Parmesan only. Use the parsley on just the first two layers so it stays green instead of going brown and bitter deep in the bake.

Cover the dishes and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with fresh parsley and a little grated Parmesan, then let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice so the layers set instead of sliding.
prose.portion_html:
This batch is built to feed 14, so portion it by weight and not by eyeball. Once the lasagna has rested, put your empty container on the scale and zero it out. Weigh the full baked dishes, divide that number by 14, and that is your target weight per container. Cut and plate to hit it, adjusting the last couple of pieces as you go.

Doing it this way is how every serving actually comes out to 496 calories with 40.7 grams of protein, 34.4 grams of carbs, and 21.4 grams of fat. Corner pieces run a little cheesier than center cuts, so the scale is what keeps everybody honest across all 14 dinners.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that makes a high-protein lasagna feel almost unfair: this whole batch breaks down to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is 14 dinners, each one carrying 40.7 grams of protein, for the kind of money that usually buys you a sad drive-thru side. Cottage cheese and no-boil noodles are doing the budget work while the mozzarella and Parmesan do the flavor work.

Cook once, portion 14 times, and the per-plate cost falls right where a real budget meal-prep dinner should. Comfort food math that finally adds up in your favor.

steps: Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken breast bites according to the package directions, then roughly chop them into bite-size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, Alfredo sauce, and a generous pinch each of salt and pepper (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper) until completely smooth.

Coat the bottom of each dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce, then layer 3 no-boil lasagna sheets, more sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and Parmesan; repeat, using parsley on only the first two layers and finishing the top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan, rest at least 5 minutes, then slice and portion into 14 servings by weight.
